findings.claim: A separate pension scheme, Jaminan Pensiun, takes another 3 percent of its members' wages, up to a ceiling (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015a); it pays a pension, so I leave it out of the growth comparison.
findings.evidence:
S: Scope: the diff of draft/.rounds/5.json against 6.json shows only one change, draft line 13, where ', up to a ceiling' was inserted. The new wording is identical in draft .md:13, .src.md:13 (bound to {{src:pp45_jp_total.values.total_pct:int}}), site MDX:22 and the .docx (word/document.xml checked).

Source integrity: sha256 of sources/text/pp_45_2015.txt is 995c021e..., and pp_45_2015.pdf is f48fe915.... Both match sources.json pp45_jp_total. I re-extracted the PDF with pdftotext -layout, and the whitespace-normalized text is identical to the stored text layer. Pasal 29 sits on PDF page 21 (lens-S/pp45_p21.txt:12-23). The reference entry (.md:135, MDX:175) URL equals sources.json fetched_from.

Clause by clause against PP 45/2015:
(a) '3 percent of its members' wages': Pasal 28(2), pp_45_2015.txt:822-823, reads 'sebesar 3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan'. BPJS IR 2025 (bpjs_ir_2025.txt:3322) still gives '3% dari upah sebulan', so the 28(4)-(5) path toward 8% has not been applied.
(b) 'up to a ceiling': Pasal 29(2), :855-858, reads 'Batas paling tinggi Upah yang digunakan sebagai dasar perhitungan Iuran Jaminan Pensiun untuk tahun 2015 ditetapkan sebesar Rp7.000.000,00 ... setiap bulan'. That is a ceiling on the wage base. 'X percent of wages, up to a ceiling' is the standard English form for a capped base. A reader who attaches the phrase to 'takes' instead (a capped contribution) gets the same result. I computed it in lens-S/jp_ceiling_check.txt: JP = 0.03 x min(wage, cap), so 3.000% of any wage at or below the cap and less above it (1.582% of Rp20m in 2025).
(c) Pasal 29(3), :859-864, adjusts the ceiling every year by a factor of 1 plus the previous year's GDP growth. The sentence says only 'a ceiling', with no amount or year, so it does not imply a fixed cap and needs no indexing qualifier. The ceiling is current: IR 2025 :3322-3326 gives 'batas upah atas tahun 2025 sebesar Rp10.547.400' with the same indexing text, and IR 2024 :9551-9552 gives Rp10.042.300.
(d) The ceiling is in the cited regulation itself (2015a), so the citation covers the new clause. The clause adds no number, so it needs no bound key. Its quote is recorded at docs/provenance-audit.md:614-617 ('JP's 3% applies to wages up to a ceiling'), which the new wording mirrors.
(e) The contrast with JHT is accurate. PP 46 Pasal 17 (pp_46_2015.txt:444-451) defines the JHT base as 'Upah sebulan ... Upah pokok dan tunjangan tetap' with no cap. The only 'batas' hits in pp_46 (:593, :595, :1008) are about benefit withdrawal. So qualifying JP alone does not suggest a cap JHT lacks.
(f) 'its members': Pasal 1 angka 4 (:68-69) defines Peserta as a worker who is registered and has paid contributions. Pasal 4(1) (:184-188) phases registration in ('sesuai penahapan kepesertaan').
(g) 'it pays a pension': Pasal 1 angka 3 (:63-66) reads 'Manfaat Pensiun adalah sejumlah uang yang dibayarkan setiap bulan'. The elucidation (:1085-1088) calls the scheme a 'program manfaat pasti'. The Pasal 24(1) lump sum (:737-742) for members with under 15 years of contributions, and Pasal 3(4)(b), are an alternative benefit. They do not contradict the clause, which does not say 'only'.

No clause misstates the regulation. Note, not new: Pasal 29(1) (:852-854) limits the base to basic pay plus fixed allowances. 'Wages' renders the regulation's own term 'Upah', just as the JHT sentence does. | L: Scope: a diff of draft/.rounds/5.json against 6.json shows that round 5 changed one thing, the insertion of ', up to a ceiling' at draft .md:13. The same text is at .src.md:13, bound to pp45_jp_total, and at site MDX:22. No other surface changed. (1) What the ceiling caps: PP 45/2015 Pasal 29(2) (sources/text/pp_45_2015.txt:855-858) says 'Batas paling tinggi Upah yang digunakan sebagai dasar perhitungan Iuran Jaminan Pensiun ... Rp7.000.000,00'. That is a ceiling on the wage the contribution is computed on. Because the phrase follows 'of its members' wages', the natural reading is wages counted up to a ceiling. The other possible reading, that the amount taken is capped, is also true: the cap times 3 percent. Either way the sentence is accurate. Pasal 29(3)-(4) (:859-866) index the cap each year, and the cap is still in force: bpjs_ir_2025.txt:3322-3326 gives '3% dari upah sebulan (dengan batas upah atas tahun 2025 sebesar Rp10.547.400 ...)', so the present tense 'takes' holds. (2) Citation: '(Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015a)' is PP 45/2015, the regulation that contains Pasal 29, so the existing citation supports the qualifier. docs/provenance-audit.md:613-617 already records the ceiling as its own entry (PDF p.21, Pasal 29(2)). (3) Consistency with the JHT sentence before it: JHT has no ceiling. PP 46/2015 Pasal 17 (pp_46_2015.txt:442-470) defines the base as monthly wage, basic pay plus fixed allowances, with no cap. PP 60/2015 amends only Pasal 26 (pp_60_2015_kemnaker.txt:70-82). So qualifying JP and not JHT matches the law, and it ends the shared-base implication round 5 found. 'Another' still reads as an additional contribution. (4) The 'so I leave it out of the growth comparison' logic is unchanged: it rests on 'it pays a pension', which design amendment line 139 supports (JP stays apart 'as a defined-benefit pension', 'program manfaat pasti'). The ceiling neither strengthens nor weakens that reasoning. (5) Licence: I ran the gate's own checks on the sentence (lens-L/check_claims.py, imported with bytecode writing off). gate.checks.claims._flags returns [] for the sentence, and claims.check on the rendered draft against gate.toml [claims] returns no failures. 'so' is not in the CAUSAL list. The numbers check's _DIGITS and _WORDS find nothing in 'up to a ceiling'. So the qualifier needs no [claims] entry, no [allow] entry and no bound key under the repo's rules, and it adds no number. Style note, not a defect: 'up to a wage ceiling' would name what is capped without relying on the reader's attachment of the phrase. | H: Diff of draft/.rounds/5.json

That evidence applies to the chart label just as it did to the sentence: in 2025, JP is 1.582% of a Rp20,000,000 wage (lens-S/jp_ceiling_check.txt). The note cites only Pasal 28 and not the Pasal 29 cap. After round 5, the prose (line 13) qualifies JP's share and the chart and its alt text do not. The project's own provenance-audit.md:63-64 says R7's 'shares of wages' holds for JP 'only below the ceiling'.

Round 1's skeptic (r1:item:337) ruled that alt text omitting a chart-note caveat is a style matter, and round 2 (r2:item:38) confirmed the alt text. JP is in no computation. (1) The rendered charts/jh-3-contributions.png (opened) shows the JP bar as '3% of pay', with x-axis 'Percent of wages' and title 'What goes in each year, as a share of pay'. Nothing on the chart mentions a ceiling. make_charts.py:161 writes every bar's label as f"{total_pct:g}% of pay". The note at make_charts.py:171 cites only PP 45/2015 Pasal 28. The project PNG and site/public/images/blog/jh-3-contributions.png are byte-identical (both sha256 4b1675fb3d73eb19...).
(2) The published copies match: the alt text at gate.toml:74 renders as 'JP, a separate pension, 3 percent' (site MDX:78), and the MDX figcaption at :79 repeats the Pasal 28-only note. results.json contributions.jp = {worker 1, employer 2, total 3}, from build_analysis.py:174 src('pp45_jp_split').
(3) The cap is in the stored statute, one article after the one the note cites. Pasal 28(2) (sources/text/pp_45_2015.txt:824-825) sets '3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan'. Pasal 29(2)-(3) (:855-863) caps the wage base at Rp7,000,000 a month for 2015 and indexes it each year. bpjs_ir_2025.txt:3322-3323 gives the 2025 cap in the same cell as the rate: Rp10.547.400.
(4) My computation (skeptic-S/jp_chart_check.txt): 2015, wage Rp20,000,000: JP = 0.03 x 7,000,000 = Rp210,000, which is 1.050% of pay. 2025: Rp316,422, which is 1.582%. So '3% of pay' is false for members paid above the cap.
(5) This is the same defect round 5 fixed in prose. r5:item:1 was adjudicated 'the cap exists, so the unqualified share is false for members paid above it', and draft .md:13 / MDX:22 now say 'up to a ceiling'. The chart directly below it in the 'What goes in' section (draft .md:50) still states the share without the cap. The project's own audit flags this chart by its claim id: provenance-audit.md:63-64 says 'R7's "shares of wages" holds ... only below the ceiling', and make_charts.py:149 labels chart 3 as R7. A grep of the design doc for 'ceiling' finds 0 hits, so no owner decision accepts the simplification.
(6) The mitigations do not clear it. 'The shares the regulations set' is literally Pasal 28(2), but the same regulation caps the base in Pasal 29, and the chart's own axis and title name the base as pay/wages. Round 1's r1:item:20 let the cap pass only because that sentence made no claim about the base; this chart does make one. r1:item:337 and r2:item:38 judged the CPF band and the 401(k) participant scope, not the JP cap, and both came before round 5 set this standard. The CPF parallel (r2:item:7) differs on the decisive point: no stored file holds the CPF ceiling, while PP 45 Pasal 29 is stored and already cited.
(7) Severity stays LOW: JP is in no computation, and no conclusion changes. Scope note: the chart was not edited in round 5. This finding is the downstream inconsistency that the round 5 fix created, so it belongs with that fix.

findings.evidence: Quoted sentence (draft .md:52, MDX:86): 'Singapore's CPF takes 37 percent of pay, worker and employer together, for workers aged 55 and under, on wages in the top band.' The same claim, with no ceiling, is in the chart 3 alt text (gate.toml:74, MDX:78: 'Singapore's CPF, 37 percent ... on wages in the top band'), the chart 3 bar label '37% of pay', and its footnote (make_charts.py:174-175). Round 5 refuted JP's unqualified share on one ground: 'the cap exists, so the unqualified share is false for members paid above it'. CPF has the same kind of cap. cpf.gov.sg 'What constitutes wages for CPF contributions' (fetched 2026-10-23) says the Ordinary Wage ceiling 'sets the maximum amount of OW that attracts CPF contributions in a calendar month', and its worked example computes contributions 'on $8,000 of Ordinary Wages'. cpf.gov.sg 'How much CPF contributions to pay' confirms 17% + 20% = 37% for age 55 and below with monthly wages above $750. 'Top band' means wages of $750 or more (dataset metadata, sources/provenance/cpf/meta_d_98ffa142ae0dec40391f78f81d26aca9.json: 'applicable for the highest wage band ... wages of $750 or more per month'). A lay reader can take 'top band' to mean high earners, the very group for whom the ceiling makes 37% false. Rounds 1 and 2 raised the OW ceiling but left it as 'not in any stored file' (round2-verdicts.json, CPF item). Before round 5 the post treated JP and CPF alike, both unqualified statutory shares. Now JP carries 'up to a ceiling', JHT correctly carries none, and CPF carries none. By contrast, a reader will infer CPF has no ceiling. A Singaporean or a pension economist could quote that as misleading for pay above the OW ceiling. The core comparison (JHT 5.7% is small next to statutory CPF) is not reversed, so severity is LOW. | skeptic: The finding stands, on the same rule round 5 used for JP. (1) The text is as the finding quotes it at draft .md:52, MDX:86, gate.toml:74, MDX:78 and make_charts.py:174-175. I opened charts/jh-3-contributions.png: the CPF bar reads '37% of pay' under the title 'What goes in each year, as a share of pay'. (2) 'Top band' is not a band of high earners. sources/provenance/cpf/meta_d_98ffa142ae0dec40391f78f81d26aca9.json says the rates 'are applicable for the highest wage band', for example 'wages of $750 or more per month'. So pay above the CPF ceiling is still in the top band. (3) The ceiling exists. I fetched cpf.gov.sg 'What constitutes wages for CPF contributions' (2026-10-23): the OW ceiling 'sets the maximum amount of OW that attracts CPF contributions in a calendar month for all employees', and its worked example computes contributions 'on $8,000 of Ordinary Wages'. cpf.gov.sg 'How much CPF contributions to pay' gives 17% + 20% = 37% from 1 January 2026 for age 55 and below, wages above $750. (4) My computation (skeptic-H/cap_checks.txt) uses the page's $8,000 example: at S$10,000 a month, 0.37 x 8,000 = S$2,960, which is 29.6% of pay; at S$15,000 it is 19.7%. My fetches did not show the 2026 ceiling amount itself, but the claim fails above any ceiling. (5) The sentence's scope is unchanged since round 1. Its context changed in round 5, and the round 6 workflow sends such claims to 'extra' (round6.js:30-31); the H lens was asked about exactly this unevenness. Round 2 (r2:item:7) let it stand only because the ceiling was 'not in any stored file'. Round 5 then ruled for JP that 'the cap exists, so the unqualified share is false for members paid above it' (round5_fixes.txt). Applied evenly, that rule covers CPF too. (6) Severity LOW is right: the paragraph's point (5.7 is small next to 37) holds below the ceiling. One part of the proposed fix breaks the fix rules. The cited data set (Central Provident Fund Board, 2026) never states a ceiling, so adding 'up to a ceiling' brings in an internet fact with no reference. That would need a new APA 7 entry for cpf.gov.sg. The finding itself says so.
